CustomEvent, bubbling, dispatched on the from-plate's <video>: gl:frame when GL engages, takes one frame and pauses the loop; gl:release when GL disengages

handoffs.change: Listen for the bubbling 'gl:frame' event from the plate's own <video>: keep the loop paused and release the DecoderLock. Listen for 'gl:release' from the same <video>: if motion is on and the plate is visible, re-acquire the lock and resume. The loop must sit inside a [data-media] that names either the loop id (registered to the plate: poster or endsOn) or the plate id. MediaFrame already does this.
handoffs.why: Review finding #4. GL now grabs the from-loop's frame when it engages at a p end, so the plate never pops when p leaves 0. Without this handoff, a loop GL paused stays frozen after release until its MediaFrame visibility changes, and the decoder is not freed.

handoffs.change: Pass choice: act.variant in each GlCardSpec.
handoffs.why: Review finding #5: GL must resolve title.mask and match.shape exactly as CARDS' css side does. GlFrame already falls back to film.acts by world, so this is belt and braces.

handoffs.change: Record a GL chunk size deviation. Measured with TS transpile, terser (module, 2 passes) and gzip -9, before Turbopack wrappers. First GL chunk (gl-lock, plan, cover, shaders, textures, transition-gl, gl-frame) is 11,691 B gz. sdf-title is its own chunk at 1,324 B gz, loaded on the first GL title (never under the title.mask ALT). gl-debug is 274 B gz, loaded under ?gl=force, ?debug=gl or /lab/ only. Facade (gl-gate + support) is 945 B gz. GL total on a full desktop scroll is about 12.8 KB gz against the 8 KB line in spec §12.1 and plan §6.2.
handoffs.why: Review finding #6. Debug and the SDF generator are now split out. A per-card shader split would shrink only the first chunk, not the total loaded over a full scroll, so I did not do it. The spec's estimate of 3–4 KB for shaders + 1.5 KB SDF did not include the lock and plan runtime, which §3.3 requires.

handoffs.change: Do not let the to-plate's DOM loop play under an engaged GL frame between a.range[1] and b.range[0], or accept the risk. GL draws the opaque settled to-still there and goes transparent at b0 (.50).
handoffs.why: P3-6 #10 risk (not part of the review). If a to-loop is playing underneath, the still-to-loop handover at p .50 can pop.

notes: FIXED #1: Job gained want() and drop(). pump drops unwanted jobs and calls drop; run errors also drop; onLost drops every queued job. A plate's ImageBitmap is closed and its loading key cleared in every path, including a lost or unwanted bitmap at fetch resolve. Plate and title jobs are wanted while ANY host needs the key, so a GlFrame remount (lab card switch) reuses an in-flight job instead of deadlocking on the dedupe. The SDF stepper job had the same bug and is fixed the same way.

FIXED #2: admit() protects the owner's keys only while the owner holds: mid-transition, or on screen with p < 1 (at p >= 1 GL draws nothing). evict() disengages an engaged host whose texture it drops; only a non-holding owner can be hit, which is offscreen or at p >= 1 drawing clear. reprep() asks again for refused near1 cards when the owner stops holding (visibility IO, owner reaches p >= 1). Without it, my first version only partly fixed the reviewer's scenario.

FIXED #3: a failed plate is no longer stored as a solid texture. Its key goes into a broken set, ready() stays false and the card stays css. The key is cleared on the next near1 approach so the fetch retries. solid: is used only for ids with no plateAsset. Failures are logged as plate:failed and failed by the lab probe.

FIXED #4: the from-video is grabbed in tryEngage at the p end, before the first draw. It must be playing, readyState >= 2, and inside a [data-media] equal to the plate or a loop registered to it, so the to-loop is never taken. The frame is drawn for p <= 0 too and released (texture dropped, gl:release) only in disengage or remove. The upload is off the motion path. The LivePlate handoff is blocking. I did not use a GL-side play() fallback because it could break the DecoderLock.
FIXED #5: GlFrame resolves both pieces with spec.choice, else film.acts by world. The lab passes choice: cfg.variant so its ALT configs preview the whole ALT card.

PARTLY FIXED #6: gl-debug and sdf-title are dynamic chunks; log and compiles are recorded only in debug. The remaining size is a recorded deviation (handoff with numbers). Not done: per-card fragment chunks (total unchanged over a full scroll).
FIXED #7: dynamic(() => import('./gl-frame').catch(() => ({ default: () => null })), { ssr:false }).
FIXED #8: free() drops every plate and title texture and clears the SDF cache when the last host is removed, and in stopAll when off. The context, noise, solids and programs stay.

FIXED #9: tryEngage waits until p has been still for QUIET_MS (a one-shot retry timer). A p move into 0<p<1 during the fade aborts it (disengage, logged 'abort', before data-gl is ever set) and re-engages at the next end. settle is logged with p, and the probe counts it in midSwitches.

FIXED #10: update() compares maskOrigin, text and world by value. titleKey (drawn) and titleWant (asked) are split: the engaged host keeps drawing the old title until the new texture is uploaded, then swaps. ready() requires titleKey === titleWant.
FIXED #11: marks are read from markIds(id): the drawn asset first, then the video id when its poster is drawn. A fallback image never borrows the planned plate's marks (follows the markOf docstring).
Rejected: none. All 11 findings were verified as real; #6 is partly fixed with a recorded deviation.
